basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 3:18 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 79. Cur spinas et tribulos germinavit terra (Gen. III, 18) ?-- Resp. Per peccatum'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 79. Cur spinas et tribulos germinavit terra (Gen. III, 18) ?-- Resp. Per peccatum enim hominis terra maledicta est, ut spinas pareret et venenosas herbas ad poenam vel [ad] exercitationem mortalium, ut ante oculos homo semper habeat originale crimen et vel sic admonitus [aliquando] se avertat a peccatis.
